title: Summon: Web3Auth open-source code for easy login to Cardano DApps

ms.promise:
Objective: Gauge potential user needs
Method: We will put out an invitation for 2 Focus Group sessions for the Cardano Community. 
・We will advertise these sessions on X (Twitter), Reddit, and the Cardano Forum. 
・We will also send specific invitation to project teams in the ecosystem that we know may want to use this tool.
・The target audience of these sessions will be open-source developers.
・The target number of attendees for this session will be 5-10.
・The sessions will be at different times of day to encourage participants from different time zones.
・While the sessions will be conducted in English, our team is distributed with members in North America, South America, and Europe with the ability to speak multiple languages. We will also activate our supporters in Asia and Africa to help spread the invitation to attend these sessions. We have specific individuals we can talk to on every continent.

Output: After the focus groups have been conducted we will write a short report with the team takeaways.
・This report will include what we have learned about user needs and how our product can best meet them
ms.criteria: A recording of the listening session and a short report outlining team takeaways and how we plan to meet user needs.
ms.report:
Milestone 1 Completion Report
To start, we had to modify our approach a bit because of the lack of response we got from the developer community to sign up for a meeting. We started by putting out an announcement to the community that we were going to be doing feedback sessions and focus groups. We put out a sign-up form and directly solicited colleagues. Here is our focus group form:
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12OGYes5ELbw7m5jovkJL2Pqcc7vxhAHodPGwtTAmdEI/edit
The general response we got was that they already knew what we were building and that they didn't need a full tour, or they didn't have time to set up a meeting. You can see that we tagged our collaborators from around the world, had a few of them repost it (and some said they privately passed it on). But there was not a large appetite to participate.
https://twitter.com/SummonPlatform/status/1767138899900641359
However, we did get two positive responses which would provide us with feedback. 1) The SpacePlace crew invited us to be on their weekly YouTube show. 2) The Cardano Foundation invited us to showcase our product to a peer group to see if they would want to implement it.
Recordings of two Feedback Sessions:
Session #1: Guest spot on “Cardano SpacePlace” YouTube show to hold project explanation and receive feedback. This was valuable because SpacePlace is already an established brand in the Cardano ecosystem so we received feedback from their established audience and Cardano users who came just to see us.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bfVOVDakK_Y
Session #2: Presentation and discussion with Cardano Foundation and Paris Blockchain Week. PBW was exploring possibilities for voting systems and we described how the Web3Auth project could be used to allow for voting that is limited to people who register their phone numbers via SMS. This was valuable because it gave us feedback on what a real-world application is looking for.
https://app.fireflies.ai/view/Summon-Web3Auth-Demo-mp4::khsQxvWX9S35UThb

Objective: Develop a basic functional prototype of the React hook.
Method: The prototype will provide full functionality for Web3Auth integration and incorporate community feedback as collected in Milestone 1.
・Review Web3Auth functionality to understand best way to integrate React hook.
・Review community feedback to understand specific needs for Cardano applications.
・Create a functional blueprint of how the product will be designed.
・Design React hook so that it optimizes integration for Cardano applications.

Output: 
・A functional blueprint on how the product is designed.
・A prototype open-source web-hook that leverages Web3Auth to allow login to Cardano dApps with Google, Twitter, Apple, etc.
ms.criteria: A functional blueprint and working prototype that can integrate Web3Auth with a sample Cardano DApp, and a video of this sample DApp in use with our hook.
ms.report:
Milestone 2 Completion Report

Link to Open Source Repository: 
https://github.com/ADAO-Summon/useCardanoWeb3Auth 
Link to DApp Demonstration Video: 
https://twitter.com/SummonPlatform/status/1785060417733021944
Functional Blueprint:
Purpose: 
・Allows integration of social logins (OAuth verifiers) for Cardano applications as promised to developers.

Primary Functions: 
・Authentication handling, social login integration, Cardano wallet operations as developers indicated they needed.

System Architecture:
・Components:
・Web3AuthProvider: Manages authentication state and interactions.
・useCardanoWeb3Auth: Hook that facilitates authentication processes.
・Interactions: 
・Interfaces with web3auth.io to leverage OAuth for authentication and wallet creation.

User Interface Design:
・The library provides backend functionalities with UI components being provided by integrating developers.

Data Models:
・User Authentication Data: Stores OAuth tokens, user credentials from social providers.
・Wallet Information: Details of Cardano wallets created or used during authentication.

Business Rules:
・Follows protocols for secure authentication and wallet creation using CIP-30 Wallet API.

ms.report:
Milestone 3 Completion Report

We completed the Beta Release some time ago and shared it across our network of collaborators! 
Link to Beta Release Announcement:
https://x.com/SummonPlatform/status/1785060417733021944 
When our Prototype was complete we labeled it as our Beta Release and shared this post across our network of Collaborators to solicit comments. Reception went well and we are currently in talks with a key Cardano institution to adopt our Web3Auth solution.
Link to Beta Release Implementation:
https://smmn.app
We can demonstrate that our Web3Auth integration Beta Release is working correctly because we have it running on the Summon Platform. Visit our site and log in with the "Continue with Google" option. This will utilize Web3Auth for a seamless connection to a wallet securely derived from the user's Google account. While we are only enabling Google login for this implementation users can take advantage of any of the Web3Auth account integrations or program their own.
Link to Open Source Repository: 
https://github.com/ADAO-Summon/useCardanoWeb3Auth 
The Open Source repository provides an nmp package to allow any Cardano developer to integrate Web3Auth services with their dApp and the source code can be inspected for quality assurance.
